title: Constructing new geometries: a generalized approach to halving for hypertopes

reading.scope: All supplied statements and proofs, introductory and concluding claims, bibliography, diagrams and toroid application cases read. Source reading is not proof acceptance. Repeated simple diagram information is also available in the text.

named_items.label: Theorem A
named_items.summary: Partitioned geometry: diagram, residual connectedness, thinness and flag transitivity under B1/B2 and a nonbipartite graph.
named_items.notes: Duplicates the Section3 conclusion; existing counterexamples concern its unrestricted residual-connectivity claim.

named_items.label: Theorem B
named_items.summary: Identify the coset geometry of the halving group with the geometric halving construction.
named_items.notes: Duplicates Theorem4.4; distinguish literal coset-isomorphism assertion from claimed hypertope preservation.

named_items.label: Proposition 2.1
named_items.summary: Distinguished involutions of a regular hypertope form a C-group.
named_items.notes: Explicit source citation[8],Theorem4.1.

named_items.label: Construction 3.1
named_items.summary: Replace vertices and edges by the two parts of a bipartite graph.
named_items.notes: Source[1],Construction6.2.

named_items.label: Construction 3.2
named_items.summary: Double the vertex type for a nonbipartite neighbourhood geometry.
named_items.notes: Source[1],Construction5.2; failure of residual connectedness motivates the new construction.

named_items.label: Lemma 3.3
named_items.summary: Adjacency exchanges the two even-walk classes when there are two.

named_items.label: Lemma 3.4
named_items.summary: Connectedness of the partitioned neighbourhood geometry follows from the even-walk class choice.

named_items.label: Lemma 3.5
named_items.summary: Gonality of the partitioned neighbourhood geometry from odd and even cycles.
named_items.notes: Nonbipartite case explicitly invokes source[1],Lemma3.6.

named_items.label: Construction 3.6
named_items.summary: Label each higher object by one of its local even-walk classes; define incidences by the stated intersections.

named_items.label: Lemma 3.7
named_items.summary: A three-object flag has a nonempty common intersection of its chosen classes.

named_items.label: Theorem 3.8
named_items.summary: Every flag of the partitioned incidence system extends to a chamber.

named_items.label: Lemma 3.9
named_items.summary: A residue at a new type0 or type1 object is identified with an old vertex residue.

named_items.label: Lemma 3.10
named_items.summary: Residues at flags containing type0 or type1 are identified with old residues.

named_items.label: Lemma 3.11
named_items.summary: A residue of cotype{0,1} is described by the intersection of the chosen local classes.
named_items.notes: Existing parity audit must be consulted before treating that intersection as one even-walk class of the full flag shadow.

named_items.label: Lemma 3.12
named_items.summary: Higher-rank residues are asserted to be partitioned or bipartite constructions on old residues.
named_items.notes: Same existing parity-compatibility obligation; no new acceptance here.

named_items.label: Proposition 3.13
named_items.summary: Unconditional residual-connectedness preservation for the nonbipartite construction.
named_items.notes: Known v1 counterexamples are recorded separately; this reading does not rerun or extend them.

named_items.label: Proposition 3.14
named_items.summary: The old chamber-transitive group acts chamber-transitively on the new geometry.

named_items.label: Proposition 3.15
named_items.summary: Swap new types0 and1 and complement the chosen local class to obtain a duality.

named_items.label: Proposition 3.16
named_items.summary: Thinness is preserved in both directions.

named_items.label: Proposition 3.17
named_items.summary: A criterion for retaining B1/B2 at another disjoint leaf, in terms of local bipartiteness.

named_items.label: Theorem 3.18
named_items.summary: Collect the diagram, residual-connectedness, group action, thinness and further-leaf conclusions.
named_items.notes: Continues on physicalpage12. Components require separate dispositions; do not reject or accept all clauses as one.

named_items.label: Theorem 4.1
named_items.summary: Bipartite construction: diagram, connectivity, group actions, thinness and other leaves.
named_items.notes: Main result from source[1],Theorem6.2; thinness argument supplied here.

named_items.label: Definition 4.2
named_items.summary: Define halving by choosing the bipartite or partitioned construction.

named_items.label: Proposition 4.3
named_items.summary: Equivalence of bipartiteness, index-two halving subgroup, parity of relators and a binary character.

named_items.label: Theorem 4.4
named_items.summary: Identify the halving coset geometry with the geometric construction.
named_items.notes: Its proof uses residual-connectedness preservation; literal isomorphism is not refuted by the existing v1 correction.

named_items.label: Lemma 4.5
named_items.summary: Express B1 by intersection of the vertex stabilizer and its conjugate.

named_items.label: Lemma 4.6
named_items.summary: A sufficient group-coset condition for B2.
named_items.notes: Left/right coset conventions require careful later proof audit.

named_items.label: Proposition 4.7
named_items.summary: Failure of B1 forces failure of the halved intersection property.

named_items.label: Example 4.8
named_items.summary: A regular polytope of type{3,3,2} illustrates B1/B2 without the stronger lattice condition.

named_items.label: Example 4.9
named_items.summary: The hemicube fails B2 while its halving group still gives the tetrahedron.
named_items.notes: The following discussion says this seems sporadic; it is not a numbered conjecture or a classification theorem.

named_items.label: Theorem 5.1
named_items.summary: Present the three regular cubic-toroid lattice families by one extra relation.
named_items.notes: Source[2],Theorem6D4; n>=3,s>=2,k in{1,2,n}. Explicit lattice bases follow.

named_items.label: Lemma 5.2
named_items.summary: The toroid vertex-edge graph is nonbipartite exactly when k and s are both odd.

named_items.label: Lemma 5.3
named_items.summary: The exceptional degenerate leaf is k=1,s=2 in the stated toroid families.
named_items.notes: Proof continues onpage17.

named_items.label: Example 5.4
named_items.summary: Odd-period three-dimensional cubic toroid and duplication of higher objects.

named_items.label: Example 5.5
named_items.summary: Even-period three-dimensional cubic toroid and bipartite construction.

named_items.label: Proposition 5.6
named_items.summary: One halving of the nondegenerate toroids is asserted regular, and opposite-end halving gives the dual.

named_items.label: Proposition 5.7
named_items.summary: All three leaves after the first halving are nondegenerate outside the two stated parameter exceptions.

named_items.label: Proposition 5.8
named_items.summary: Present the halving groups for odd k and s.
named_items.notes: Two explicit relator families k=1 and k=n; Tietze proof continues onpage19. Exact formulas need full later verification.

named_items.label: Proposition 5.9
named_items.summary: Present the index-two halving groups when k or s is even.
named_items.notes: Reidemeister-Schreier derivation onpage20; keep its full relator data.

named_items.label: Corollary 5.10
named_items.summary: The opposite end of the once-halved toroid has a bipartite truncation.

named_items.label: Proposition 5.11
named_items.summary: Present the twice-halved groups for n>4.
named_items.notes: Five parameter/parity cases; statement continues onpage21.

named_items.label: Proposition 5.12
named_items.summary: Present the twice-halved groups for n=3.
named_items.notes: Five parameter/parity cases, square Coxeter diagram.

named_items.label: Proposition 5.13
named_items.summary: Present the twice-halved groups for n=4.
named_items.notes: Four parameter cases, four-leaf Coxeter diagram.

unnumbered_principal_claims.claim: Previously published polytope-halving theorem for the lattice/nondegeneracy hypothesis, cited to source[18].
Explicit bases for each translation lattice family.
All iterated halving diagrams up to duality for n=3,4,5 and n>=6; the text asserts the remaining leaves are nondegenerate without providing each calculation.

informal_observation.summary: The hemicube exception to necessity of B2 is described as apparently sporadic.
informal_observation.classification: informal observation; no asserted complete classification
